quarterly_data.quarter: Marvell press release: Marvell Bolsters Connectivity Portfolio with New 3.2T (10-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Marvell announced two 3nm copper-interconnect devices for AI scale-up, both now sampling to customers: (1) the Alaska E 3.2T protocol-aware Ethernet / UALink / ESUN retimer - 3.2 Tbps aggregate bandwidth via 16 224G PAM4 SerDes lanes, 45dB+ insertion loss compensation, for on-board and backplane XPU-to-XPU and XPU-to-switch links; (2) the second-generation Alaska A 1.6T AEC DSP, moved to the 3nm node - eight lanes of 224G PAM4, 12.8W in a 12mm x 14mm package (known good die format available), eight-watt power savings compared to 5nm designs, copper reach exceeding six meters (double the first-generation product). Both are integrated into Marvell's RELIANT interconnect telemetry platform. Xi Wang (SVP and GM, Connectivity Business Group): 'AI scale-up networks are moving rapidly to 224G signaling'; the expanded Alaska portfolio gives hyperscalers 200G/lane retimer options across boards, backplanes and active electrical cables. The release carries supporting statements from UALink (board chair Kurtis Bowman of AMD), Amphenol (AECs leveraging Marvell AEC DSPs) and Molex (backplanes and AECs; 'we look forward to continuing to work with Marvell').
